title: How Did Warfare Work in the Iliad?
gist: A short podcast-episode note previews a discussion with historian Josho Brouwers, author of 'Warlords of Greece: Warfare in Homer's World,' on how Homeric warfare actually worked and what the aristocratic warrior ethos of the Iliad and Odyssey reveals about ancient Greek combat.

insights.claim: Josho Brouwers' book 'Warlords of Greece: Warfare in Homer's World' examines what the Iliad and Odyssey reveal about the warrior ethos that dominated the ancient Greek and Roman imagination and how battles were actually fought in the world of Achilles, Hector, and Odysseus.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: No direct market relevance; useful only as a historical/cultural reference point, not an actionable signal.

insights.claim: The episode's discussion centers on the role of the aristocratic class, the importance of personal honor and wealth, the tactics of ancient Greek warfare, and the involvement of the gods in shaping how combat was depicted.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: None for investing; a purely historical/interpretive framework for reading the Iliad's battle scenes.
